reviews.title: Replenishment
reviews.text:
It is inconvenient that users are required to pre-load money into an account balance rather than simply having the exact amount for parking debited directly from a bank account. Furthermore, charging a transaction fee every time a user replenishes their balance feels unreasonable. While a fee like 5 cents may seem small to individual users, charging it across your entire user base adds up significantly and feels predatory.

I strongly urge you to reconsider this payment structure and offer a direct, fee-free payment option for the actual time parked.

reviews.title: Unnecessary Set Refill Price
reviews.text:
It is ridiculous that you need to refill the account every time you reach a “low balance”. It makes more sense for me to pay as I park, instead of being forced to pay a minimum of $25 to reload my account , because my account balance is 50¢ short of what I need to park at that point.

I’m not always driving into the city, because trains exist. When I do, it’s out of necessity, for vet visits, doctors appointments, etc. I shouldn’t have to reload this app with that much when I only need to pay $1.75, $2, heck, $5 total for parking at any given time. With congestion zones being a thing now (another scam) and the city already charging an arm and leg to go anywhere, this forced minimum shouldn’t be a thing. The cost of living here is high as it is. Why make it worse for people just trying to get by.

reviews.title: It will log you out every time
reviews.text:
The ParkNYC app is honestly one of the most frustrating apps I’ve had to deal with. In theory, it’s supposed to make parking easier, but in practice it does the opposite.

Almost every time I try to set parking time, the app logs me out right in the middle of the process. You go through the steps, enter everything, and then suddenly you’re kicked out and forced to log back in. That alone is annoying, but it gets worse because logging back in is not quick or seamless—it’s clunky, slow, and sometimes doesn’t even work on the first try.

On top of that, the app fails at one of its most basic responsibilities: reminders. There’s no reliable notification before your meter expires, which defeats the entire purpose of using a digital parking app. If you forget to manually check, you’re basically set up to get a ticket.

The overall experience feels glitchy and poorly maintained. Buttons lag, sessions drop, and the interface doesn’t feel stable. At times, it almost feels like the inconvenience benefits the system more than the user—because if people can’t extend their time easily or don’t get notified, they’re more likely to get fined.

For something that people rely on daily in a city like New York, this level of unreliability is unacceptable. The app needs serious improvements in stability, user experience, and basic functionality.

reviews.title: No favorite zone feature
reviews.text: They took away one of the best features in the old system. The ability to add frequently used zones as favorites so when you go there the zone number is already available to select and not have to input it every time. I see no improvements in the new app and I see they took away a key feature from the old system. Why did they take a giant step backwards? Will they ever bring it back? The notification feature of when the time is about to expire does not work at all. It worked on the old system. My question to you is how can you take a perfectly good well thought out system and replace it with this junk system and say it’s new and improved? I wish there were no stars in the rating! ☹️

reviews.title: Constantly Logged Out – Extremely Frustrating App
reviews.text:
I’m honestly fed up with this parking app. Every single time I open it, I’m logged out and have to go through the entire login process again. It’s incredibly frustrating, especially when you’re in a hurry and just trying to pay for parking.

A basic feature like staying logged in shouldn’t be this hard to get right. Instead of being convenient, the app creates unnecessary stress and delays. What’s the point of using an app if it wastes more time than it saves?

Until this issue is fixed, I can’t recommend this app to anyone. It needs serious improvement.

reviews.title: Flaws that they are not willing to work with you on
reviews.text: I have 4 vehicles in the app. On this one occasion, I accidentally paid for parking on the wrong vehicle. I tried to contact ParkNYC about switching it to the correct vehicle or canceling the remainder of the session and they told me “No, there is nothing they can do” and that I have to start a new session for the other vehicle. So basically the app is ok with stealing my money and bullying me into paying for 2 session when they were informed that it is one vehicle parked and the wrong vehicle was paid for. I guess I will go back to using my card at the meter and carrying quarters  because then the receipt from the meter will go in the car I am driving and accidents like that won’t happen again.

reviews.title: Another parking app? In this economy???
reviews.text:
I hate all these parking apps. I’m left standing on a street in the dark and cold fighting with an app because there was no offline way to pay the meter! I’m not from here, i try to not drive into nyc, i usually take the subway! Plus, this one would not let me set up “pay per transaction” when i downloaded it, so i had to use their “e-wallet” and preload $25 to my account in order to pay $3 to park.

This aint Dunkin Donuts - unless you’re giving me points toward free coffee (or free parking), i shouldn’t have to pay in advance (and don’t say it’s ok since EzPass does it — they shouldn’t be allowed to do this either). Ugh!

Cell service is not reliable enough to keep requiring folks to use apps to interact with the physical world.

reviews.title: It’d be a scam if it wasn’t the “official” one
reviews.text:
The app is buggy, it intentionally logs you out, seemingly to create the potential for not having paid for your parking yet by the time the meter cop rolls by.  In Queens there are a couple parking zones that don’t show up automatically on the app, so you have to type them in.  As you may know if you pay for parking in the wrong zone, even if the zone is across the street and the identical price of the zone you’re in, they can give you a ticket. It’s very clear that this app is designed to allow those mistakes to happen.

I would say the biggest issue with the app is that it intentionally logs you out, so sometimes when you want to extend the time you have to burn extra time logging back in so that increases the chance of them catching you in the one minute before you’ve renewed your parking because you were too busy logging back in.

reviews.title: Works for the most part
reviews.text: I parked at the municipal parking lot by the staten island ferry, and paid this app for the whole day. Somehow, I still got a ticket because I didn’t display a receipt on the dashboard. I couldn’t get the parking ticket dismissed even though I paid “WinIt” to fight it. After looking up this issue, I found someone in reddit that had posted about this same issue years ago. I now only use this when I really have no other choice. I purposely park in areas past 7PM so I won’t have to pay for parking, park in different streets, or leave my car at home. The customer service was pointless and said I should not have gotten a ticket, which is gaslighting because they require that you post a paper receipt at the parking lot I was referring to. Therefore, I should not have had the option to pay using this app for that particular parking lot. One star for robbing me of my money. I’m active duty but I got a parking ticket on Veteran’s day. What a joke of company you have ParkNYC.

reviews.title: Good idea, frustrating execution
reviews.text:
This is a well-intentioned app with a good concept, but the execution is really frustrating. Every single time I open the app to check or review any type of parking information, I’m logged out and have to sign in again. It makes quick tasks unnecessarily time-consuming.

On top of that, depending on where you’re parking, there’s an extra $0.20 service fee. That might not sound like much, but it adds up—and it’s confusing and feels unnecessary for a city-run parking app.

Overall, the app has potential, but the constant logouts and added fees seriously hurt the user experience.
